title: typed SDK sync/async interop and compatibility roadmap for Python/TS/Go
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Customers are integrating Redwood SDKs across Python, TypeScript, and Go and expect idiomatic sync/async patterns, stable wire compatibility, and a clear deprecation path for breaking surface changes. This PRD defines the product requirements, language-specific ergonomics, compatibility rules, and acceptance criteria for a minimal-breaking rollout that supports streaming, paginated fetches, and retry semantics across both synchronous and asynchronous call sites.

Goal: Deliver a coordinated SDK release that: (1) provides typed interfaces for sync/async interop, (2) defines a version negotiation strategy for streaming frame schemas, (3) standardizes retry and idempotency primitives, and (4) supplies migration tooling + acceptance tests for backward compatibility across hosted and Dedicated runtimes.
scope:
In scope:
- Formalize API shape for streaming (server->client frames) and paginated responses across Python/TS/Go.
- Define compatibility matrix and semantic versioning rules for SDKs.
- Implement a thin client shim in each language to expose both sync and async ergonomics where idiomatic.
- Add end-to-end acceptance tests exercising pagination, retries, and streaming fallbacks against runtime-compat staging.
- Docs and migration guide.

Out of scope:
- Large refactors to kernel/runtime.
- New model features unrelated to client protocol.
- Full sync wrappers for every async-only language pattern (we provide shims only where safe).
requirements: Wire compatibility: all streaming frames must include a 1-byte schema_version then a frame_type token; newer schema versions may add optional fields but must be ignorable by older SDKs.
Pagination: provide an opaque page_token string; servers may return additional metadata but must not require client-side parsing. Support both page-size and cursor-limited enumerations.
Retries: SDKs must expose a RetryPolicy object (max_attempts, backoff_ms, idempotency_strategy). Default policy must be conservative (3 attempts, exponential backoff).

Sync/Async ergonomics: Python must support both sync generators and async async-generators for streaming results; TS must support AsyncIterable plus a Promise-based fetch; Go must provide channels and context-aware iterators.
Idempotency: for mutating endpoints (if any), SDKs must accept an optional idempotency_key and propagate it to the wire. Default is no key.
Telemetry: SDKs must emit optional debug telemetry hooks for retries, backoffs, and streaming reconnects (configurable opt-in).
Compatibility: maintain backward-compatible behaviors for two prior SDK minor versions; any breaking change requires a documented migration path and feature-flagged rollout.
language_specific_requirements: Python: provide a single high-level client class with methods that return either (a) synchronous generator (Iterator[Chunk]) when used normally, or (b) async generator (AsyncIterator[Chunk]) when called from async context. The client must detect active event loop and route to async core. Type hints must use typing.AsyncIterable and typing.Iterator.

TypeScript: provide both Promise-based and AsyncIterable-based surfaces. The main fetch method should be an object with .stream() returning AsyncIterable and .fetch() returning Promise<Page>. Provide strong types for Page<T> and StreamEvent<T>.

Go: provide context-aware iterators that return a typed struct per event and a Stop() method; streams should be exposed as receive-only channels. Ensure API avoids goroutine leaks on cancellation via context.Context. Provide clear guidance for memory/buffer sizing.
wire_compatibility: Schema negotiation: the first byte of a stream payload is schema_version; client and server must support fallback to a 'compat mode' for schema_version 1 and 2. Servers will advertise max_supported_schema in the connection handshake header. Any addition to frame payloads MUST use optional TLV-like fields so older SDKs can skip unknown fields. Compatibility tests will include malformed/unknown-fields fuzzing.
acceptance_criteria: API contracts: unit and integration tests for every public method surface in Python/TS/Go with type checks (mypy/tsc/go vet).
Backward compat: run compatibility matrix (latest SDK vs runtime staging, previous two SDK minor versions) and confirm no unexpected schema errors for streaming and paginated endpoints.
Retry behavior: simulate transient 500/timeout failures and assert SDKs honor RetryPolicy defaults and allow overrides. Verify idempotency_key propagation where applicable.

Stream resume/fallback: when connection resets mid-stream, SDKs must attempt an automatic resume using last-known offset where the server supports resume, else fall back to graceful reconnect and surface a RecoverableStreamError. Tests must assert at-most-once vs at-least-once semantics per documented endpoint.
Docs and migrations: publish migration guide and language-specific quickstarts; at least two customer-facing examples converted from prior SDK usage patterns.
test_plan: Unit tests: language-native unit coverage for all new surface areas (target >= 85% for new modules).
Integration: nightly e2e tests against runtime-compat staging that exercises pagination, streaming, retries, and schema negotiation.
Fuzzing: send randomized TLV optional fields and unknown frame types to verify graceful skipping.
Performance: confirm streaming overhead is < 8% compared to current raw binary client for median payload sizes; pagination round-trips remain within 2x of direct HTTP fetch baseline.
rollout: Phase 1 (Canary): release SDKs behind feature flag and enable on 5 internal customers and 2 early partners. Monitor errors, retry rates, and telemetry hooks.
Phase 2 (Gradual): Increase to 25% of new signups and opt-in existing heavy SDK users for migration helper. Collect migration failures and docs friction metrics.
Phase 3 (GA): Flip default on for all new SDK installs and provide a deprecation window of 90 days for older client helpers with automated compatibility shims where possible.
migration_notes: Provide CLI tool 'rw-sdk-migrate' that scans code for common anti-patterns (manual cursor parsing, custom backoff loops) and suggests replacements. For Python, offer a compatibility adapter that translates legacy iterator-based streaming into the new typed generator with a deprecation warning. Track migration adoption via telemetry opt-in.
